chunks: Ya'qub ibn 'Uthaym asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام and said:

He said to him: There is a well of water in whose water there is an odor, and pieces of skins are brought out from it. So he said: “It is of no consequence. The gecko sometimes sheds its skin. Only one bucketful is sufficient for you regarding that.”

key_terms.الْوَزَغَ: the gecko, mentioned as an animal that may shed its skin
key_terms.بِئْرُ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.دَلْوٌ وَاحِدٌ: one bucketful, the amount deemed sufficient to remove
key_terms.رِيحٌ: an odor or smell present in the water
key_terms.قِطَعُ جُلُودٍ: pieces of skin found coming out of the well
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water, the subject of the purity ruling here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water that has an odor and contains pieces of shed skin?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a well in which an odor is found and pieces of skin are drawn out. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that this does not render the water unusable in itself, explaining that the skin may be shed by a gecko, and that removing a single bucketful is sufficient.
